content: The Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) was developed in 2009 to evaluate the role of diet-induced inflammation in the development of cardiovascular disease. This concept was based on the established link between inflammatory states and cardiovascular disease. The components of the Dietary Inflammatory Index are designed to measure the inflammatory or anti-inflammatory potential of foods. Higher scores on the index indicate a greater anti-inflammatory effect of the foods consumed. The index has also been adapted and scored for use in population-based studies. The DII has been associated with cardiovascular disease, as demonstrated in the PREDIMED study. Additionally, the index has been linked to colorectal cancer in two observational studies. However, in one of these studies, the association was found to be statistically significant only in men.
